newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-INTERVIEW-MIM says no to copper hedge.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-INTERVIEW-MIM says no to copper hedge.

text.p: Australia's MIM Holdings Ltd is increasingly placing its fortunes in copper but refuses to hedge its output, chief executive officer Nick Stump told Reuters.

Stump said he is not convinced the miner, whose operations are based at Mount Isa in north-western Queensland, needs to hedge the hundreds of thousands of tonnes of copper it produces each year despite what he calls the "Sumitomo fiasco".

The Japanese trading house Sumitomo Corp has been at the centre of a market and regulatory scandal that sent world prices tumbling in June when it revealed US$1.8 billion in copper losses, due to the activities of former principal trader Yasuo Hamanaka, who is now under investigation.
"There are as many people that think the price is going to creep up as there are those who think it will creep down," Stump said in an interview.
